label: Input phase from the 3rd original token through <DEL>
explanation: Fires on the input (reading) side of the sequence: original-phase steps from position 2 onward, and on the <DEL> delimiter step (rate 0.73, about 20% of mass). Almost silent on the first two original tokens (t=0,1) and on the whole copy phase (0.2% rate, 0.1% of mass). Within the window the rate falls off for later positions (0.80 at t=2 down to about 0.28 at t=8). It fires less on tokens that repeat an earlier input (in_first=0), but requiring in_first lowers F1, so this is not part of the predicate. The largest activations, close to max, land on <DEL> and the steps just before it in short sequences whose first tokens are x/t/c (first_tok lift 1.3x). Low quartile: weak activations spread over long sequences. Dev: P 0.73, R 0.97, F1 0.83, mass recall 0.99.

issues: The positional window itself checks out. The predicate (phase<=1)&(t>=2) gives dev P 0.735, R 0.967, F1 0.835, mass recall 0.992. The copy phase has a 0.002 rate and 0.1% of mass. <DEL> has a 0.727 rate and 20.2% of mass. Rates at t=0 and t=1 are 0.033 and 0.091.

The claim that the rate falls with position (0.80 at t=2 to 0.28 at t=8) is a confound. The by-t table mixes original, <DEL> and copy steps. Conditioned on the original phase, the rate stays roughly flat: orig_idx 2..8 gives 0.805, 0.784, 0.732, 0.677, 0.645, 0.671, 0.712. Scoring (phase==0)&(orig_idx==8) gives P 0.71. Within the window, to_go==0 gives P 0.70 and to_go>=3 gives P 0.77. There is no strong decay.

The claim that it fires less on repeated tokens (in_first=0) is also a confound. The low overall in_first=0 rate comes from copy-phase steps, which all have in_first=0. Inside the window, in_first==0 gives P 0.738 and in_first==1 gives P 0.736. Repetition makes no difference.

The explanation misses a systematic content gate set by the first original tokens. Precision inside the window by first token: first_tok=b gives 0.0008, so the feature is completely silent on sequences that start with b. Other first tokens: z 0.31, l 0.37, m 0.50, versus 0.94 for the group {x,t,c,o,n,1,r,2,y,v,f}. The second token matters too: orig(1)=b gives 0.21 and orig(1)=t gives 0.96. The test-split false positives are whole silent sequences, not scattered noise, and that matches this gate.
Calling the first_tok effect a modest 1.3x lift on top activations understates it. It is a hard gate for b and a large modulation for the other first tokens.
skeptic.revised_label: Input phase from the 3rd original token through <DEL>, gated by the identity of the first two tokens (silent when the sequence starts with b)

final_label: Input phase from the 3rd original token through <DEL>, gated by the identity of the first two tokens (silent when the sequence starts with b)

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: x, t, c, o, n, 1; least: m, l, z, b) and the second original token (most: t, c, x, n, 1, o; least: w, m, l, b); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, phase=1.
